To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

- the latest prototype sensors have shown excellent performances in terms of charge collection, noise and efficiency; - the radiation hardness of the devices has been demonstrated to be compatible with the requirements of the experiment;

the SuperB Silicon vertex tracker will be realized using thin hybrid pixel detectors, with a pixel pitch of 55x55 micron^2, a sensor thickness of 150 micron and a total material budget of about 0.2% X0/X0.

(1) thin hybrid pixels are very robust and show excellent performance, but are difficult to realize with the current technology, (2) CMOS MAPS are very promising and show excellent performance and radiation hardness, but need to be further developed to be fully radiation hard, and (3) INMAPS and Vertical Integration MAPS have excellent performance and are radiation hard but have not yet been tested at the level of the other technologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and characterization, in the laboratory and in the beam, of pixel devices to be employed in the inner layer of a tracking system for the future SuperB experiment.
the design and development of the most advanced pixel detectors for the SuperB silicon vertex tracker.
the development of pixel detectors based on thin, high resistivity, low leakage current, radiation hard devices featuring a very low power consumption and a very low noise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SuperB collaboration is well advanced in the development of a silicon pixel vertex detector for the innermost layer.
the CMOS MAPS technology is the most promising one for the SuperB vertex tracker.
all technologies are promising but the choice will depend upon the final requirements of the SuperB detector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pixel detector for SuperB is a very challenging project, but we are confident that the final result will be a state of the art device, fully compatible with the SuperB requirements.
all the technologies investigated are promising, but none of them is ready for a final design.

we have demonstrated that the SuperB Silicon Tracker will be able to cope with the very demanding requirements imposed by the SuperB environment and the very high luminosity foreseen for the SuperB collider.
The main takeaway from our work is that
all options can be considered for a successful realization of the SuperB vertex tracker.
the SuperB Silicon Tracker will be the first pixel detector in which a pixel sensor with a pixel pitch as small as 50μm will be used.
all the investigated technologies are promising and can be used to satisfy the SuperB requirements.
